newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST -Australian Sports News - Nov 20.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST -Australian Sports News - Nov 20.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

The West Indies want to bury any recent ill-feeling between their side and Australia by restarting the old tradition of after-play dressing room drinks. Team manager Clive Lloyd and coach Malcolm Marshall approached Australia's coach Geoff Marsh about the decision earlier this week. Page 26.

US golfer Tiger Woods had two air swings during the pro-am lead-up to tomorrow's A$1 million Holden Australian Open. His coach Butch Harmon was a little concerned, offering McDonalds as a bribe if Woods could shoot four-under on the back nine. Page 26.

Former gold medal hockey winner Nova Peris has shown she may be a medal hopeful in another discipline, clocking only 12.19 seconds over 100 metres in Melbourne. Peris has already attended one interclub meeting this season and looks strong in her new field. Page 25.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Soccer Australia will pay its new national coach Terry Venables A$420,000 a year for his services. Venables will only spend four months of the year in Australia as his job also requires him to monitor the performance of European based Australian players. Page 54.

Tiger Woods has agreed to return to Australia next year to play in the Australian Masters and a Skins game in Queensland. Woods will play in the A$1 million Australian Open which starts tomorrow. Page 54.

Australia's 1997 Super League draw hopes to hold a re-match of the 1994 Brisbane-Wigan world club championship game. Other clubs set to visit Australia in the competition include London, Halifax, Oldham and Leeds. Page 54.
THE AGE

The appointment of Terry Venables as the national coach of Australia's soccer team yesterday came as a shock to many. Venables is the former coach of England and took the job on with the prospect of leading the Socceroos into the 1998 World Cup. Page C16

Mark Philippoussis has sacked his sixth coach since he joined the ATP Tour at the beginning of last year, with Peter McNamara the latest to fall. John Newcombe and Tony Roche have been redrafted to prepare him for the Hopman Cup, the Australian Open and the Davis Cup. Page C16.

International Management Group's Australian chief, James Erskine, has offered golfing sensation Tiger Woods the opportunity to play into two IMG events - the Skins at Coolum on the Gold Coast and the Masters in early February. Page C16.
HERALD SUN

Robert Allenby is fighting a bout of the flu in a bid to play in the Australian Open, which starts tomorrow. This new illness compounds Allenby's lack of practice lately, but he has said that he will "play with a broken leg" if he has to. Page 86.

Closer relations are hoped for between cricketing rivals Australia and the West Indies, with the West Indian team management initiating peace talks with the view to improving off-field rapport with the Australian side. Relations between the two teams hav been tense over the last ten years, but last year's Caribbean tour has brought about an improvement. Page 86.

Bendigo will join the new Victoria Football League in 1998 with a team made up of players from around its region. Bendigo Gold and Bendigo Bulls are two of the names that have been suggested for the club so far. Page 85.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Terry Venables has taken on Australia's top soccer job as the new head coach of Australia's national soccer team. Venables took on the job because of his desire to take part in a national team's efforts in the World Cup. Page 80.

Touch football has been given a boost with a new national "Super Touch" league being launched as the result of a A$1 million sponsorship deal that will be announced today. The three-year deal with Liptonice is the largest in the sport's history. Page 78.

Dean Capobianco, the sprinter accused of taking anabolic steroids at the Atlanta Olympics this year, will argue that he may have tested positive to the drug after consuming meat contaminated with the drug. His hearing is to be held in Monte Carlo on Sunday night. Page 78.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
